reading.body:
The only fact here is a job title: Melva Wallace leads Huston-Tillotson University, and the dataset files her under AI advocates without recording any AI work.

The record rests on a single LinkedIn profile. It carries no secondary sources, no dates of birth or death, no nationality, and a timeline whose one entry reads "Current" rather than a year. What it establishes is a position, president and CEO of a historically Black university in Austin, Texas, and a field, higher education administration. What it does not establish is any AI teaching, research, procurement, or policy engagement by her or by the institution.

That gap is the point of the category. Advocates and Public Voices is where an ecosystem map records who speaks about AI and on what authority, and here the authority is institutional leadership in higher education. A reader cannot tell from this data whether Huston-Tillotson trains AI workers, hosts compute, or holds any position on the technology at all. The entry marks a possible voice, not a documented one.

Nothing in the data touches compute, buildings, or power. Austin appears only as a location inside a job description, with no facility, load, or grid fact attached to it. The inclusion of a university president says more about how the advocate category is drawn than about AI in Austin.
